key_insight: A ternary-solvent growth strategy produces large-area hybrid perovskite monolayers, enabling lithography-free optoelectronic devices with ultra-low static power.
engineering_relevance: Larger ultrathin crystals support direct shadow-mask contacts, avoiding solvent-based lithography that can degrade perovskites.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents and an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Use molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations to probe solvation and growth mechanisms.
Fabricate planar devices from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels using physical shadow masks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports (PEA)2CuCl4 monolayer areas exceeding 1000 µm² and (PEA)2PbI4 devices with approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, 250-fold below drop-cast films, and a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates optoelectronics, not AI or solar-cell performance; manufacturing yield and long-term device stability remain unspecified.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
